Metastatic spinal tumor: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance, severe cord compression, and an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements are suggestive of a metastatic spinal tumor.
Spinal lymphoma: The presence of a diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension causing severe cord compression, in the absence of a known primary malignancy, could also suggest spinal lymphoma.
